en fil.explanation: "En fil" means "a file" on a computer. It is also a metal tool for smoothing things, like "en neglefil" (a nail file).

en filial.explanation: "En filial" means "a branch", as in a branch of a company. To say a company opens one in another town: "Vi åbner en filial i Odense" (We are opening a branch in Odense). Do not mix it up with "en afdeling" (a department): "Jeg arbejder i salgsafdelingen" (I work in the sales department).

en film.explanation: "En film" means "a film". To say more than one, add no ending: "Vi har set to film" (We have seen two films). To ask if someone has seen a film, use "set" (seen): "Har du set filmen?" (Have you seen the film?)

en filmaften.explanation: "En filmaften" means "a movie night". It is built from "film" (movie) and "aften" (evening). To suggest one, ask: "Skal vi have filmaften i aften?" (Shall we have movie night tonight?)

en filmstjerne.explanation: "En filmstjerne" means "a film star". It is built from "film" (movie) and "stjerne" (star). To talk about stars in the sky, use the same word "stjerne": "Der er mange stjerner i aften" (There are many stars tonight).

en filosof.explanation: "En filosof" means "a philosopher". To say what a person studies, use "filosofi" (philosophy): "Hun læser filosofi" (She studies philosophy).

en finale.explanation: "En finale" means "a final", as in the last match of a competition. To say a team gets that far, say: "De nåede finalen" (They reached the final). To talk about the big last part of a concert, use the same word: "Koncertens finale var flot" (The finale of the concert was beautiful).

en finanslov.explanation: "En finanslov" means "a national budget". It is built from "finans" (finance) and "lov" (law). In Denmark, the parliament "Folketinget" passes it each year.

en finger.explanation: "En finger" means "a finger". To say your finger hurts, Danish says "the finger" where English says "my finger": "Jeg har ondt i fingeren" (My finger hurts), literally "I have a pain in the finger".

en finne.explanation: "En finne" means "a fin". Another meaning is a person from Finland. To say someone is one, say: "Min ven er finne" (My friend is a Finn).

en firewall.explanation: "En firewall" means "a firewall". The word comes from English. To say you switch it off, use "at slå fra" (to switch off): "Slå firewallen fra" (Turn the firewall off).

en firkant.explanation: "En firkant" means "a four-sided shape". It is built from "fire" (four) and "kant" (edge). The part "kant" also appears in "en bordkant" (a table edge).

en fisk.explanation: "En fisk" means "a fish". In the plural, "fisk" has no ending: "tre fisk" (three fish). To say what you eat, use "at spise" (to eat): "Vi spiser fisk til middag" (We eat fish for dinner).

en fiskefrikadelle.explanation: "En fiskefrikadelle" means "a fish cake". It is built from "fisk" (fish) and "frikadelle" (a Danish meatball). A classic Danish dish is "fiskefrikadeller med remoulade" (fish cakes with remoulade, a cold sauce).

en fiskehandler.explanation: "En fiskehandler" means "a fishmonger". It is built from "fisk" (fish) and "handler" (a dealer). The word also means the shop itself. To say you go to the shop: "Jeg skal ned til fiskehandleren" (I am going down to the fish shop).

en fisker.explanation: "En fisker" means "a fisherman". To say what a fisherman does, use "at fange" (to catch): "Fiskeren fanger torsk" (The fisherman catches cod). Do not mix it up with "en fiskehandler" (a fishmonger): "Fiskehandleren sælger frisk laks" (The fishmonger sells fresh salmon).

en fiskerby.explanation: "En fiskerby" means "a fishing village". It is built from "fisker" (fisherman) and "by" (town). The part "by" also appears in "en storby" (a big city).

en fiskestang.explanation: "En fiskestang" means "a fishing rod". The last part "stang" (pole) also appears in "en flagstang" (a flagpole). In the plural, the vowel changes: "to fiskestænger" (two fishing rods).

en fjende.explanation: "En fjende" means "an enemy". To talk about an enemy that two sides share, say: "en fælles fjende" (a common enemy).

en fjer.explanation: "En fjer" means "a feather". In the plural, "fjer" has no ending: "tre fjer" (three feathers). To say a pillow is filled with feathers: "en pude med fjer" (a pillow with feathers).

en fjernbetjening.explanation: "En fjernbetjening" means "a remote control". It is built from "fjern" (far) and "betjening" (operation). "Betjening" also means "service", as in "god betjening" (good service).

en fjord.explanation: "En fjord" means "a fjord". In Denmark, "Limfjorden" is a fjord in northern Jutland.

en flagermus.explanation: "En flagermus" means "a bat", as in the animal. Literally, it is "flutter mouse", from "flagre" (to flutter) and "mus" (mouse). To say more than one, add no ending: "to flagermus" (two bats).

en flagstang.explanation: "En flagstang" means "a flagpole". The last part "stang" (pole) also appears in "en fiskestang" (a fishing rod). In the plural, the vowel changes: "to flagstænger" (two flagpoles).
